paper.title: Retroformer: Retrospective Large Language Agents with Policy Gradient Optimization
paper.central_claim: Fine-tuning a plug-in retrospective language model with policy gradient on the change in episode return, while keeping the actor LLM frozen, yields better reflections that raise success rates over ReAct and Reflexion on HotPotQA, AlfWorld and WebShop.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker in this subagent context; model_type is the configured type only. Component-training boundary: retained state is reflector weights plus per-task reflection text.

sections_read: Appendix A-E (challenges, intuition, implementation details, reward functions, additional experiments, prompt examples referenced)

evidence.quote: This paper introduces a principled framework for reinforcing large language agents by learning a retrospective model, which automatically tunes the language agent prompts from environment feedback through policy gradient.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: a small retrospective model that rewrites the actor prompt is trained by policy gradient from environment return; the actor LLM stays frozen.

evidence.quote: Note that the only learnable parameters are in the retrospective model
evidence.support_explanation: Retained learned state is the retrospective model's weights (LoRA r=1 or 4, 0.53M or 2.25M parameters); reflections are appended to the actor prompt as per-task long-term memory.

evidence.quote: Hence, the difference in episode returns between two consecutive trials naturally serves as a reward signal for fine-tuning the retrospective model
evidence.support_explanation: Reward for the improver: next-trial return minus current return (delta reward), credited to the reflection that preceded it.

evidence.quote: Because the actor is a frozen LM and the temperature is low as default
evidence.support_explanation: Attribution assumption: with a frozen low-temperature actor, differences in returns are attributed mostly to the reflection; environment noise and task difficulty are not otherwise controlled.

evidence.quote: For offline training, we collected the dataset
evidence.support_explanation: Training is offline: rollouts of the base policy on training-set tasks, then SFT on positively rated samples, a reward model and PPO.

evidence.quote: In online execution, we use best-of-
evidence.support_explanation: At inference a learned reward model reranks best-of-n reflections; n and its cost are not given in the main text.

evidence.quote: The agent is evaluated on 100 validation tasks from the distractor dev split of open-source HotPotQA dataset, 134 tasks in AlfWorld and 100 tasks in WebShop, as in
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation sets: 100 / 134 / 100 tasks; no repeated runs, so 1 task = 1 point (1%) on HotPotQA and WebShop.

evidence.quote: This agent enhances from verbal feedback of the environment, but does not use gradient signals explicitly.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline Reflexion uses the actor-class LLM as the reflector; no frozen LongChat reflector or SFT-only variant appears in Table 2 (rows: SAC, ReAct, Reflexion, Retroformer r=1, r=4).

evidence.quote: uses a much larger frozen language model, i.e., GPT-3 (model: text-davinci-003) as the reflection component.
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the baseline reflector is a much larger frozen model than the 7B fine-tuned retrospective model, so the contrast conflates model identity with gradient training.

evidence.quote: Our Retroformer agent achieves 54% success rate in 4 trials, which is better than the state-of-the-art 50% success rate reported in
evidence.support_explanation: HotPotQA GPT-3: Retroformer 54% vs Reflexion 50% (n=100). Table 2 also: GPT-4 54% vs 52%; ReAct 34%/40%.

evidence.quote: Retroformer agents improve the success rate in HotPotQA by 18% with 4 retries, 36% in AlfWorld with 3 retries and 4% in WebShop
evidence.support_explanation: Headline gains; the baseline for 18%/36%/4% is unspecified and the numbers do not match a single contrast in Table 2 (e.g. HotPotQA 54 vs 34 = +20 over ReAct, +4 over Reflexion).

evidence.quote: The results probably indicate that the verbal feedback approach (Reflexion, Retroformer) is not an optimal method for this environment, but our fine-tuning method still proves effective.
evidence.support_explanation: WebShop gain is small: 36 vs 35 (GPT-3), 45-46 vs 44 (GPT-4) on 100 tasks, inside binomial noise.

evidence.quote: In all experiments, we set the temperature of actor LM as zero, i.e., T=0 and top p =1 to isolate the randomness of LM from the effects of reflections.
evidence.support_explanation: Design choice to isolate reflection effect; single deterministic actor run per task.

evidence.quote: we collected 523 reflection samples
evidence.support_explanation: Training data are small (HotPotQA 3,383 samples from 3,000 train tasks; AlfWorld 523; WebShop 267); whether AlfWorld/WebShop training tasks are disjoint from the 134/100 evaluation tasks is not stated.

evidence.quote: The number of trainable parameters is 0.53M
evidence.support_explanation: LoRA r=1: 0.53M trainable parameters (r=4: 2.25M), trained with PPO after SFT and reward modelling.

evidence.quote: All experiments are done in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) GKE environment with A100 40GB GPUs.
evidence.support_explanation: Only hardware type is given; no GPU-hours, data-collection cost, reward-model or best-of-n inference cost.

evidence.quote: We plan to open source the code repository after the review period.
evidence.support_explanation: Code unavailable at the pinned version (anonymous link only).

evidence.quote: our approach is not limited to enhancing the retrospective model alone
evidence.support_explanation: Authors claim the method can tune other components (memory, summariser, actor prompt); not tested.

evidence.quote: The long and short-term memory components provide context that is specific to a given task
evidence.support_explanation: Reflection memory is per task across retries; lessons are not stored or retrieved across tasks.

evidence.quote: It can serve as a baseline for showing the effectiveness of gradient-based learning.
evidence.support_explanation: SAC (2.25M params) provides an online-RL baseline with constant success (27% HotPotQA); not budget-matched.

signatures.object: retrospective model (LongChat-7B + LoRA) that produces reflection text appended to the frozen actor's prompt
signatures.information: full failed trajectory (states, actions, rewards), previous reflections; environment return; frozen actor behaviour
signatures.operation: sample 2 reflections per failed training task (T=0.9), roll out the next trial for each, label higher next-trial return as accepted; train SFT on positives, a reward model on accepted/rejected pairs, then PPO
signatures.conditions: frozen low-temperature actor assumed to isolate reflection effect; binary/F1/soft rewards per environment
signatures.selection_rule: pairwise preference by delta return; best-of-n by reward model at inference
signatures.selection_data: base-policy rollouts on training tasks; evaluation on separate validation tasks
signatures.persistence: LoRA weights (offline) + per-task reflection memory appended to prompt within an episode
signatures.later_use: trained reflector writes reflections for held-out tasks across up to 4 retries
signatures.claimed_effect: higher success after N retries than ReAct/Reflexion on HotPotQA, AlfWorld, WebShop
signatures.failure_boundary: WebShop gains small; frozen reflector baseline absent; delta reward noisy

signatures.operation: append reflection to actor prompt for the next trial
signatures.conditions: retry allowed with environment success feedback
signatures.failure_boundary: not transferred to other tasks; this is a retry mechanism

gap.author_gap: Frozen LLM reflectors give uninformative verbal feedback (credit assignment failure) and Reflexion-style agents do not learn from environment rewards via gradients.
gap.checked_gap: Partially confirmed: one qualitative failure example (Fig 1/5) and Reflexion baseline plateau; no measurement of reflection quality or ablation of reflector identity.
lineage: Reflexion / Self-Refine -> verbal self-feedback from a frozen LLM
RLHF/PPO/DPO tooling -> weight updates for text generation
Retroformer -> RL-fine-tune a small reflector on delta return, keep the actor frozen
closest_adjacent: RL-trained prompt editors (e.g. RLPrompt/TEMPERA-style) are not cited or compared
gap.residue: Reflection quality improvable by reward-driven training without touching the actor weights.
gap.stakes: Faster learning across retries and better final success on multi-step tasks.
gap.method_response: Treat actor as environment, train reflector with PPO on delta return and a reward model.
gap.remaining_gap: No frozen-small-reflector or SFT-only control, retries not separated from transfer, noisy delta reward, small evaluation sets, no cost accounting.
unresolved: Reflexion/Self-Refine/RAP and RL prompt-editing originals not pinned; Table 1 is the authors' capability checklist.

claims.text: Retroformer reaches 54% on HotPotQA after 4 retries, beating Reflexion (50% GPT-3, 52% GPT-4) and ReAct
claims.setting: GPT-3/GPT-4 actors, LongChat-7B LoRA retrospective, 100 dev tasks
claims.result_denominator: n=100, single run, +4/+2 points over Reflexion
claims.counterevidence: difference to Reflexion within one binomial SE
claims.allowed_conclusion: Comparable to or slightly above Reflexion; ahead of ReAct.

claims.selection_vs_test: train tasks (523 reflection samples) vs 134 evaluation tasks; overlap not stated
claims.allowed_conclusion: Large improvement over Reflexion on AlfWorld in this setup; disjointness unstated.
No reliable gain over Reflexion on WebShop.

claims.text: Policy-gradient fine-tuning of the retrospective model is what produces better reflections and learning speed
claims.counterevidence: no frozen/SFT-only reflector; headline 18/36/4 numbers unreconciled with Table 2

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A LoRA-fine-tuned 7B reflector trained offline on base-policy rollouts improves success after up to 4 retries on held-out AlfWorld tasks relative to Reflexion with a larger frozen reflector (100% vs about 85%), with only small, noise-level gains on HotPotQA and WebShop; causal credit to policy-gradient training itself is not isolated.
unresolved: Headline 18%/36%/4% do not map to a single Table 2 contrast.
AlfWorld/WebShop train-eval disjointness unstated; benefit is within-task retries not cross-task transfer.

G.reason: The limitation (frozen reflectors cannot assign credit; verbal feedback not tuned by reward) is real and illustrated, and Reflexion/Self-Refine/RAP are positioned, but evidence for the bottleneck is one qualitative example, RL-trained prompt editors are not covered, and the remaining-gap boundary is not stated.

M.reason: Clear mechanism: treat the frozen actor as environment, credit the reflector with next-trial return change, build preference pairs, train a reward model and PPO. Assumptions (reflection explains return change, low-temperature actor) are stated; confounds of task difficulty and noise are not addressed.

X.reason: Training pipeline and hyper-parameters are given, but inference-time best-of-n details, reward-model data size, evaluation retry protocol and code are missing; no acceptance check before deploying a fine-tuned reflector, no versioning or rollback, and reflection memory is only per task.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmark success rates with fixed evaluators and fixed actor temperature; HotPotQA metric (EM vs F1) for "success" and the headline 18/36/4 numbers are not fully specified.

E.causality.reason: ReAct, Reflexion, SAC, LoRA ranks and two actors give partial attribution, and AlfWorld shows a large effect, but the key controls are absent: frozen or SFT-only small reflector, best-of-n only, and reflection transfer across tasks; Reflexion uses a different, larger reflector.

E.holdout.reason: Offline training on training-set rollouts with evaluation on separate validation tasks; sample sizes for AlfWorld/WebShop training and their disjointness from the evaluation tasks are not stated and cross-task transfer is not tested.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs on 100/134/100 tasks without intervals or seeds; several headline gains (HotPotQA +4/+2, WebShop +1/+2 over Reflexion) are within sampling noise.

E.cost.reason: Only parameter counts and GPU type; data-collection, reward-model, PPO and best-of-n inference costs and the retry budgets per method are not compared.
